sections.st: Three Problems Hygiene Product Thermoformed Trays Buyers Face

strips.title: Packaging Contamination — Hygiene Products Require Clean Packaging
strips.desc: Problem: Baby hygiene products (cotton pads, wipes, swabs) are skin-contact items — packaging contamination transfers to the product surface and potentially to baby skin. Standard thermoforming production environments may not provide adequate particulate cleanliness for hygiene product packaging. Solution: ISO 9001:2015 documented production with controlled material handling and clean production environment for all baby hygiene packaging. BPA-free materials confirmed per batch.

strips.title: BPA-Free for Skin-Contact Hygiene Products
strips.desc: Problem: Baby hygiene products are applied to sensitive infant skin — packaging in contact with hygiene products must be free from BPA and phthalate plasticisers that could migrate to the product surface. Solution: BPA-free PP and BPA-free APET as standard for all baby hygiene packaging. Material CoA confirming BPA-free per production batch.

strips.title: Moisture Compatibility — Hygiene Products in Humid Environments
strips.desc: Problem: Baby wipes and wet cotton products generate moisture inside the packaging that affects packaging material performance over product shelf life. Solution: PP is the preferred material for moisture-exposed baby hygiene packaging — PP has very low moisture absorption and maintains dimensional stability in humid packaging environments.

sections.st: Hygiene Product Thermoformed Trays — Key Design Requirements

strips.title: Clean Production Environment — ISO 9001:2015 Controlled
strips.desc: Baby hygiene packaging production under ISO 9001:2015 controlled procedures — documented material handling, production equipment cleaning, and final inspection before dispatch. ISO 9001:2015 batch documentation per run confirms production conditions for each baby hygiene packaging batch.

strips.title: Moisture-Compatible PP — For Wet Hygiene Product Applications
strips.desc: PP is preferred over APET for baby wipes and wet hygiene product packaging — PP has very low moisture absorption (0.01–0.03%) compared to APET (0.1–0.3%), maintaining tray geometry and dimensional stability in the moist product environment over shelf life.

strips.title: Crystal-Clear APET for Retail Hygiene Display
strips.desc: For retail-facing baby hygiene product packaging (cotton swab display, cotton pad retail packs), APET crystal-clear thermoforming provides the product visibility that drives retail purchase. APET is selected for dry hygiene product packaging where moisture compatibility is not required.

strips.title: Dispensing Compatibility — Wipe Tray Geometry for Pop-Up Dispensing
strips.desc: Baby wipe tray geometry must be designed for compatibility with the pop-up dispensing mechanism — the tray must hold the wipe stack in correct orientation for sequential dispensing without tangling or stack collapse during the product shelf life.

faqs.q: Why is BPA-free mandatory for baby hygiene product packaging?
faqs.a: Baby hygiene products are applied to sensitive infant skin. BPA and phthalate plasticisers in packaging materials can migrate to product surfaces and contact infant skin. BPA-free PP and APET packaging eliminates this migration risk. Material CoA per production batch confirms BPA-free status for skin-contact compliance.

faqs.q: Why is PP preferred over APET for baby wipes packaging?
faqs.a: PP has very low moisture absorption (0.01–0.03%) compared to APET (0.1–0.3%). For wet baby wipes and moist hygiene products, PP maintains tray geometry and dimensional stability in the moist packaging environment over shelf life. APET is selected for dry hygiene product retail display applications.

faqs.q: What materials are used for baby hygiene packaging trays?
faqs.a: BPA-free PP (primary — wet hygiene products, wipes, bulk OEM hygiene trays), BPA-free APET (retail display hygiene packaging requiring crystal clarity), BPA-free PETG (premium baby hygiene gift set packaging). Material CoA confirming BPA-free status per production batch.
